bugs: StoreWebhookEventRequest.php:17 uses 'data' => ['required','array'], so a correctly signed event with an empty data object ({}) gets a 422 and is never stored. A probe confirmed it returns 'The data field is required.'. The provider will keep redelivering an event that can never be accepted.
README.md: the webhook docs are added below the untouched Laravel boilerplate README instead of replacing it.
routes/console.php:12: the daily model:prune has no onOneServer(), so on multi-server deployments every server runs it.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:106 `$order->markPaid($details) && $order->user->notify(...)` uses short-circuit && on a void call to get conditional side effects inside a match.
app/Models/Order.php:46 json_encodes payment_details by hand because transitionTo() goes around the model's array cast with a query-builder update.
app/Console/Commands/RedispatchStuckWebhookEvents.php plus the stuck scope and a 5-minute schedule add recovery machinery the task did not ask for (over-engineering).
database/migrations/2026_01_01_00000*.php: none of the migrations has a down() method.
routes/webhooks.php is loaded through a `then:` callback with an empty Route::group, which is extra ceremony for one route.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:93 calls Validator::make inside the job to re-validate the stored payload, so validation happens in two places.
strengths: Order::transitionTo makes an atomic conditional UPDATE, so out-of-order or concurrent events cannot overwrite a later state.
Refunds are deduplicated by the provider's refund_id, and a test covers the same refund arriving under a different event id.
Modern job attributes (#[Backoff], #[MaxExceptions], #[Timeout]) with retryUntil, WithoutOverlapping and a RateLimited Limit::perSecond(10).
The rate-limit test drives the real RateLimited middleware 12 times and asserts 10 pass and 2 are released, rather than only checking configuration.

Handles 429 with Retry-After, fails permanently on 4xx and rethrows 5xx and connection errors. A database-queue probe showed backoff of 5/30/120/300, then failed() marking the event failed with the error.
The receipt notification implements ShouldQueueAfterCommit and is sent inside the transaction.
Uses the #[Signature]/#[Description] command attributes, #[Scope], #[Fillable] and MassPrunable.

bugs: Order::refund (app/Models/Order.php:63-70) moves an order to Refunded from any state, including Pending, and keys the Refund on the webhook event_id instead of a provider refund id. The same refund delivered under two event ids would create two refunds.
bootstrap/app.php sets apiPrefix '' and puts the webhook route in routes/api.php, so 'api/' has to be typed into each API route. It works, but the route layout is unusual.
antipatterns: tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:170 builds the rate limiter's internal key by hand (md5('payment-provider'.'payment-provider')), and :147 builds the WithoutOverlapping lock key by hand. Both couple the tests to framework internals.
app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:14 adds Model::shouldBeStrict, an app-wide change outside the task's scope.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:82-105 signals 'released' by returning null from fetchDetails, which is a slightly awkward control flow.
tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:181-188 reads the #[Backoff] attribute by reflection to test backoff, which tests configuration rather than behaviour.
strengths: A clean pipeline: VerifyPaymentSignature middleware fails closed when no secret is set, the invokable controller uses createOrFirst plus wasRecentlyCreated for exactly-once storage, and duplicates return 200 'duplicate'.

The job uses the #[Timeout], #[MaxExceptions], #[Backoff] and #[DeleteWhenMissingModels] attributes with retryUntil, WithoutOverlapping keyed by event_id and a named RateLimited limiter. A database-queue probe showed backoff of 10/30/60/120, then the event marked failed with the error and one row in failed_jobs.
A PermanentWebhookFailure exception with $this->fail() cleanly separates permanent errors (4xx, no matching order) from retryable 5xx errors, and 429 Retry-After is honoured.
Re-reads the event with fresh() and checks isFinished(), locks the order row with lockForUpdate, uses state-guarded markAsPaid, and queues the notification with ShouldQueueAfterCommit.

The daily pruning schedule uses onOneServer() and withoutOverlapping. The README is rewritten with thorough guidance on deploying workers: shared cache, nested timeouts, queue:restart, not passing --tries.

Broad Pest coverage: signature edge cases, validation datasets, an end-to-end test, a lock-held test, a rate-limit-exhausted test, 5xx then success with withFakeQueueInteractions, and the policy and pagination.

v.rationale: Both implementations pass their own suites (impl-2: 43 tests, impl-1: 42). Both also passed a database-queue probe: repeated 503s gave increasing backoff, then failed() marked the event failed with the error. Both pick the same modern Laravel 13 tools: job attributes, WithoutOverlapping, a RateLimited perSecond limiter, createOrFirst, MassPrunable plus model:prune, and ShouldQueueAfterCommit notifications. impl-2 ranks first. Its intake is more tolerant: a signed event with empty data is accepted, while impl-1 returns 422 for it, which a probe confirmed. impl-2's permanent-failure handling (a custom exception plus fail()) is cleaner, its schedule uses onOneServer, and its README is a focused rewrite where impl-1 appends to the boilerplate. It also avoids impl-1's extra ceremony: the redispatch-stuck command, the separate webhooks route file, the void `&&` trick inside match, and hand-written json_encode around the model's casts. impl-1 still has real merits: atomic conditional state transitions, refunds deduplicated by provider refund_id, and a behavioural rate-limit test. impl-2's weaker points are that refunds are keyed by webhook event id and have no state guard, and that some tests depend on framework-internal cache keys.
